what: AST SpaceMobile is building satellites large enough to connect directly to an ordinary mobile phone, so a normal handset gets a signal anywhere, with no special hardware.
customers: Mobile operators such as AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone and Rakuten, who would resell the coverage to their own subscribers.
moat: Patents on very large phased-array satellites and signed agreements with mobile operators covering billions of subscribers, who would rather partner than build their own.
risks: $1.8B of negative free cash flow and a $628M net loss: the constellation is still being built
72 times sales on $143M of revenue, nearly all of it pre-commercial
The whole business depends on launching dozens more satellites on schedule and on them working
opportunities: $4.3B of cash against $2.2B of debt, which funds the next phase of the build
Revenue grew from $14M to $71M last year as early service began
Analysts see about 148% upside, with 12 covering the stock; direct-to-phone satellite coverage would be a genuinely new market
watch: Satellites launched and working, and whether operator agreements convert into paid service.
